results.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem belongs to NP.
results.proof_sketch: Let L be the total number of feature occurrences. Every non-teleport move deletes at least one feature from each of two tiles, so a play contains at most L/2 moves. Moreover, an unordered tile pair cannot be used twice: its first move deletes every feature then live on both endpoints, and deleted occurrences never return. Thus a certificate is a polynomial-length tile sequence. Simulating the moves, checking that every transition has a live common feature, applying all simultaneous deletions, and checking that no occurrence remains takes polynomial time.

results.claim: There is an exact characterization by perfect matchings plus an ordered Euler trail with precedence constraints.
results.proof_sketch: For feature f, let S_f be its occurrence tiles. Choose a perfect matching M_f of S_f, and let H be the simple union of all M_f. For v∈S_f write m_f(v) for its matching edge. Then a solution exists exactly when H has an Euler-trail ordering τ such that, for every nonmatching edge e=uv of H with u,v∈S_f, either τ(m_f(u))<τ(e) or τ(m_f(v))<τ(e). Necessity follows because deletion moves for f form a perfect matching, every move deletes some feature, and a nonmatching move joining two f-tiles can occur only after at least one occurrence was deleted. Conversely, scan τ. The condition inductively ensures that every matching edge meets two still-live occurrences, while every nonmatching edge has an already-deleted endpoint for f. Hence precisely the M_f edges delete f. Since every H-edge belongs to some M_f, every transition is non-teleport, and all occurrences are deleted.

results.claim: If every occurring feature appears on exactly two tiles, no-teleport solvability is decidable in linear time even with unbounded sharing number.
results.proof_sketch: Construct a simple graph K on the nonempty tiles, placing edge uv whenever at least one feature occurs exactly on u and v. Multiple such features on the same pair are collapsed into that edge, so sharing can be arbitrarily large. Every edge of K is mandatory: its represented features have no other possible partners. Conversely, when uv is traversed for the first time, all features represented by uv are still live and are deleted together. Therefore a play is exactly an Euler trail of K. The instance is solvable iff K is connected after isolated empty tiles are discarded and has zero or two odd-degree vertices. Building K, testing connectivity, and counting odd degrees takes O(L) expected time with hashing, or polynomial deterministic time after sorting endpoint pairs.

results.claim: The obvious static relaxation—choosing feature-perfect-matchings whose simple union is Eulerian—is not sufficient.
results.proof_sketch: Use five tiles 0,…,4 and features with supports {0,1}, {0,2}, {1,2}, {0,1,2,3}, and {0,1,2,4}. The first three force all edges of the core triangle 012. Tiles 3 and 4 contain only one feature each, so they must be the initial and final tiles. If the endpoint edges attach to different core vertices, the transition graph has four odd vertices; hence both attach at one core vertex i. Starting at 3, the play must take 3i, traverse the triangle as a circuit based at i, and finish with i4. But the first triangle edge out of i deletes the feature supported on {0,1,2,4} at i, making i4 impossible. The reverse direction is symmetric. Nevertheless, choose matchings 03+12 and 04+12 for the two four-occurrence features; together with forced edges 01,02,12 their union is connected and has only odd vertices 3 and 4. Thus the precedence condition in the preceding characterization is essential.

results.claim: An exact state-space algorithm runs in O(n^2 L·2^L) time and O(n·2^L) space.
results.proof_sketch: Represent the live feature occurrences by an L-bit mask and memoize states (current tile, live mask). For each of n possible next tiles, compute the features live at both endpoints; if this intersection is nonempty, clear both corresponding occurrence sets and recurse. Try every starting tile. There are at most n·2^L states, at most n transitions per state, and intersections/deletions take O(L) time in a direct representation. Acyclicity follows because every transition strictly decreases the number of live occurrences.

final_writeup:
Let S_f denote the tiles containing feature f. The principal progress is an exact separation of the static and temporal parts of the problem. Static feasibility requires selecting a perfect matching M_f on every S_f such that their simple union H is connected and has zero or two odd vertices. That is necessary because the moves deleting any one feature pair all its occurrences, and the complete move sequence is an edge-simple Euler trail of H.

It is not sufficient. The missing ingredient is an ordering constraint: whenever an H-edge joins two f-tiles that are not matched to each other, at least one endpoint’s matching edge must already have occurred. This yields the exact ordered-matching characterization stated above. The five-tile construction proves that this temporal requirement cannot be discarded, even when the static union has an Euler trail.

The characterization immediately recovers a broader tractable regime not covered merely by bounding sharing number. If every feature has frequency two, its matching is forced and there are no nonmatching edges inside its two-vertex support. Consequently all temporal constraints disappear, and the problem reduces to an ordinary Euler-trail test after parallel feature pairs are collapsed. Pairwise sharing may be arbitrarily large in this regime.

Thus the full polynomial-time-versus-NP-hard classification remains unresolved here. What is established rigorously is NP membership, an exact combinatorial reformulation exposing the source of difficulty, a linear-time unrestricted-sharing special case, an exact exponential algorithm, and a concrete obstruction to the most natural polynomial relaxation.
